name: Paula Modersohn-Becker
bio: Paula Modersohn-Becker was a German Expressionist painter and draftswoman of the late 19th and early 20th centuries. She is noted for the many self-portraits, including nudes. She is considered one of the most important representatives of early expressionism, producing more than 700 paintings and over 1000 drawings during her active painting life. She is recognized both as the first known woman painter to paint nude self-portraits, and the first woman to have a museum devoted exclusively to her art. Additionally, she is believed to be the first woman artist to depict herself pregnant.

paintings.title: Self-Portrait at 6th Wedding Anniversary
paintings.story: Self-portrait at 6th wedding anniversary, also known as Self-portrait on the sixth wedding anniversary and Self-portrait on the sixth anniversary of marriage, is a painting by the German expressionist painter Paula Modersohn-Becker during her stay in Paris in 1906.
facts: In February 1906, Modersohn-Becker moved to Paris from Worpswede, a small town near near Bremen, Germany.
She had decided to leave her husband and Worpswede forever, and devote herself entirely to art.

paintings.title: Portrait of Rainer Maria Rilke
paintings.story: The Portrait of Rainer Maria Rilke is an oil and tempera on cardboard painting by Paula Modersohn-Becker, from 1906. It is held in the Ludwig Roselius Museum, in Bremen.
facts: The Austrian poet Rainer Maria Rilke and the painter Paula Modersohn-Becker had been close friends since around 1901.
In 1902, however, he didn't mentioned her, nor his own wife, Clara Westhoff, in his art book Worpswede über die Künstlerkolonie , about an artists colony.

paintings.title: Self-Portrait Looking Slightly Left
paintings.story: Self-Portrait Looking Slightly Left is an oil on paper painting by German artist Paula Modersohn-Becker, from 1906. It is held in a private collection.
facts: The painting became the best selling of the artist when it sold by €1,270,000 ($1,159,872) at Grisebach auction house, in Berlin, well above the €250,000–€350,000 estimate.
The self-portrait is of very small dimensions and depicts the artist head and neck, as she is looking slightly from the left of the viewer.

paintings.title: Self-Portrait with Hat and Veil
paintings.story: Self-Portrait with Hat and Veil is an oil on canvas painting by the German Expression painter Paula Modersohn-Becker, from c. 1906-1907. It hangs in the Kunstmuseum, in The Hague.
facts: It has been described as an impenetrable, secret painting: "the artist stands in front of a draped window, her face both in shadow and covered by a veil, doubly concealing the backlit figure from public viewing.

paintings.title: Old Peasant Woman
paintings.story: Old Peasant Woman is an oil on canvas painting by German artist Paula Modersohn-Becker, from 1907. It is held at the Detroit Institute of Arts.
facts: Despite the old age of the sitter, the painting seems to have been inspired by the Annunciation.
" The painting was acquired by the Hamburger Kunsthalle, in 1919.
